$about: The one source of truth for Common Tools design tokens. build.mjs renders it into CommonKit's Tokens.swift and the site's tokens.css; README.md explains the layers and the rules.

secondary.about: Supporting text: ledes, captions, footers, table headers.

inverse.about: Text on an accent fill or over media.

card.about: A card or panel resting on the base surface. macOS has no card colour, so the apps tint the base with a little of the text colour.

media.about: Behind a poster or video while it loads. Nothing is written on it.

chrome.about: Translucent bars that sit over content, blurred. In the apps this is a system material, not a colour.

overlay.about: A control floating over media, in either appearance.

accent.about: Links, focus, and the active state. The user's accent colour on macOS.

accent-fill.about: A filled button. One blue in both appearances so text.inverse keeps its contrast; macOS draws its own buttons.

border.about: Rules between sections and table rows.

danger.about: An error, or a destructive action.

success.about: Something that is going well: charging, allowed, done.

contrast.about: Text and background pairs a test holds to WCAG AA (4.5:1) in both appearances, on the web values. Pairs over a system colour or over media are the system's, or unknowable, and are left out.

sans.about: The system face. The apps use Font.system; the site asks the browser for the same.

display.about: Large headings on the site; SF Pro Display is tighter above 20px.

type.about: The site's scale, named after the macOS text styles it stands in for. The apps use the system text style itself, so Dynamic Type and the user's settings keep working; only the site sets sizes.

space.about: One scale for padding, margin, and gap, in points.

radius.about: Radius, in points. xs is for small raised pieces such as a key cap; sm and up for cards and panels.

elevation.about: Shadows, by what casts them. The apps cast none of their own: windows, menus, and popovers get the system's.

motion.about: Durations in milliseconds and easings. Both surfaces drop to zero when the user asks for reduced motion.

layer.about: Stacking order on the site. Windows and menus stack themselves on macOS.

layout.about: Widths in points. The settings window and the menu panel are the apps'; the rest is the site's.
